Operator:
Good day, and welcome to the Nimbus Cloud Corporation Q3 FY2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are in listen-only mode. After the presentation, we will conduct a question-and-answer session. To ask a question, you will need to register by pressing star one one on your telephone keypad. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Alex Rivera, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Alex Rivera:
Good afternoon, everyone, and thank you for joining us. Today, we will be discussing Nimbus Cloud Corporation's results for the Q3 FY2024. With me on the call are Sarah Chen, Chief Executive Officer; Michael Patel, Chief Financial Officer; Dr. Elena Vasquez, Chief Technology Officer; Jordan Lee, Chief Product Officer; Taylor Kim, Chief Marketing Officer; Ryan Brooks, Chief Sales Officer; Lisa Wong, Chief Security Officer; and Dr. Raj Singh, Chief Innovation Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that today's call contains forward-looking statements. These statements are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a complete discussion of these risks.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Sarah Chen.

Sarah Chen:
Thank you, Alex, and good afternoon, everyone. Thank you for joining us today. Nimbus Cloud Corporation delivered exceptional results for the Q3 FY2024, demonstrating the strength of our cloud platform and the increasing demand for our AI-driven solutions across diverse industries.

During the quarter, we focused on eight key strategic priorities: expanding our global reach through strategic partnerships; driving innovation in edge computing and IoT solutions; enhancing our commitment to open source technologies; strengthening our data privacy and compliance programs; investing in our employees' professional development; improving our operational efficiency through automation; fostering a diverse and inclusive workplace; and accelerating the adoption of sustainable cloud practices.

I'm thrilled to share our standout results, which underscore our leadership in the hyperscale cloud market amid robust demand for AI workloads, hybrid architectures, and sovereign data solutions. Let's dive into our key achievements before outlining the strategic priorities that will propel us into FY2025 and beyond.

First, on financial performance: We delivered Q3 revenue of $28.7 billion, up 32% year-over-year and 8% quarter-over-quarter, handily exceeding our guidance midpoint. This marks our 15th straight quarter of accelerating growth, driven by a potent mix of consumption-based usage from AI training and inference, alongside expanding annual contract values in enterprise deals. Operating income hit $10.2 billion, with an adjusted operating margin of 38.5%, expanding 220 basis points year-over-year, reflecting the high gross margins of our IaaS and PaaS offerings, now at 72% overall, bolstered by efficiencies in our custom silicon fleet.

Remaining performance obligations reached a record $180 billion, up 45% YoY, with current RPO growing 52%, signaling strong multi-year commitments. Free cash flow was $9.8 billion, up 28%, giving us ample dry powder for our $75 billion capex plan this year, focused on data center expansions.

Customer metrics tell an even more compelling story. We added 1.2 million net new active customer accounts, bringing our total to over 85 million, including 48,000+ enterprise customers with $1M+ in trailing-12-month spend, up 22% YoY. Dollar-based net revenue retention held steady at 118%, with expansion in high-value AI and analytics workloads offsetting minor contractions in legacy storage amid customer optimizations. Compute usage surged 55% YoY, fueled by generative AI; we processed over 15 trillion GPU hours on our Nimbus AI Accelerator instances, comparable to the scale of AWS Trainium or Google TPUs.

Product-wise, our Nimbus AI Platform crossed a major milestone: It now powers 35% of Fortune 500 inference workloads, with customers like a leading automotive OEM achieving 40% cost savings versus on-premises NVIDIA A100 clusters through our auto-scaling reservoirs. We launched Nimbus EdgeForge, our fully managed edge computing service, which saw 150% QoQ adoption in telco and retail verticals for low-latency 5G/AR use cases. Security remains a differentiator—our zero-trust Nimbus Shield blocked 2.7 trillion threat events last quarter, earning top marks in Forrester's Wave for Cloud Security.

Regionally, growth was broad-based. The Americas drove 42% YoY revenue expansion to $14.1 billion, anchored by U.S. public sector wins under sovereign cloud mandates. EMEA grew 38% to $8.2 billion, with standout traction in Germany and France via our EU Data Boundary compliance, outpacing Azure's regional growth per Synergy Research. APAC was the star at 52% YoY to $6.4 billion, led by hyperscaler migrations in India and Japan; we captured 15% market share in Japan's cloud market, per IDC, through partnerships with SoftBank for Arm-based Graviton-like instances.

Sustainability achievements are noteworthy too: We hit 100% renewable energy matching for our global footprint ahead of schedule, with PUE averaging 1.15 across 45 active regions—better than Google's 1.10 target—and offset 2.5 million metric tons of CO2 via carbon removal credits.

These results position us with approximately 33% global cloud market share, per Canalys Q3 estimates, widening our lead over Azure at 22% and Google Cloud at 11% in IaaS/PaaS.

Looking ahead, our priorities are laser-focused on capturing the $1.2 trillion cloud TAM by 2028, as projected by Gartner, amid the AI supercycle and multi-cloud proliferation. We're accelerating AI and ML innovation with $30 billion in FY2025 capex for 500 exaFLOPS of new AI capacity, including next-gen Nimbus Quantum chips with 4x inference throughput over H100s. Expect launches like Nimbus GenAI Studio, integrating fine-tuning akin to Azure OpenAI, and agentic AI tools for enterprise automation. Partnerships with NVIDIA and AMD will ensure supply chain resilience, targeting 60% AI revenue mix by FY2026.

We're expanding hybrid and sovereign cloud footprint, with 70% of enterprises now multi-cloud per Flexera's State of the Cloud Report. We're doubling down on Nimbus Hybrid Core, our Kubernetes-orchestrated platform rivaling Anthos, with 25% QoQ bookings growth. Sovereign cloud builds in 12 new regions—including Australia and Brazil—address data residency needs, aiming for 20% EMEA/APAC revenue from these by year-end.

Driving cost leadership and sustainability, facing FinOps pressures, our Nimbus Optimizer tool delivered 25% average savings for 5,000+ customers last quarter via spot instances and rightsizing. We'll pioneer carbon-aware scheduling, dynamically routing workloads to green energy zones, targeting net-zero Scope 1&2 emissions by 2030.

Deepening vertical and partner ecosystems, enterprise adoption is accelerating—up 30% in healthcare and manufacturing via HIPAA/GDPR-compliant services. Key wins include a $2B, 5-year deal with a Big Four bank for core banking migration. Ecosystem expansions with Snowflake for data warehousing and ServiceNow for ITSM will unlock $10B in joint pipeline.

In summary, Q3 validates our flywheel: innovate relentlessly, scale globally, and deliver unmatched economics. We're raising FY2024 revenue guidance to $112-113 billion and operating income to $40.5-40.8 billion.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Michael Patel to provide a detailed overview of our financial performance.

Michael Patel:
Thank you, Sarah. We are very pleased with our financial results for the Q3 FY2024. Revenue increased by 32% year-over-year to $28.7 billion, exceeding our guidance for the quarter. Our gross margin was 72%, driven by our efficient cost management and economies of scale. Our operating margin was 38.5%.

I'll now turn to our overall gross margin trends and drivers, which continue to reflect the strength of our cloud platform amid accelerating demand for AI workloads and hyperscale infrastructure. For the quarter, we delivered a consolidated gross margin of 32.8%, up 160 basis points year-over-year and 40 basis points sequentially. On a non-GAAP basis, which excludes stock-based compensation and certain amortization, this expands to 33.5%. This marks our 11th consecutive quarter of gross margin expansion, underscoring the leverage in our business model as we scale to meet global demand.

Key trends and drivers start with the revenue mix shift toward high-margin services. AI and machine learning services, including our flagship Nimbus ML Platform and generative AI APIs akin to those powering models like Llama 3 or GPT-4 integrations, now represent 28% of total revenue—up from 18% a year ago. These workloads carry gross margins north of 55-60%, materially lifting the overall profile. In contrast, our core IaaS storage and compute, which still comprise about 45% of revenue, operate at 25-30% margins but benefit from pricing discipline. We've held firm on list prices while offering volume discounts tied to multi-year commitments, similar to AWS's Savings Plans or Azure Reservations, which now account for 65% of our committed spend.

Infrastructure efficiency and utilization gains are next. Data center utilization reached 87% this quarter, up from 82% YoY and a record high, driven by our optimized fleet management. We've accelerated deployment of our custom Nitro silicon—our Arm-based Graviton4 processors, which deliver 40% better price-performance than x86 alternatives—and integrated them across 70% of our EC2-equivalent instances. This has reduced power consumption per workload by 25% and lowered TCO for customers running inference at scale. Additionally, our renewable energy procurement hit 75% of total usage, mitigating electricity cost volatility, which has spiked 15-20% in some regions due to data center boom. These initiatives mirror efficiencies seen at peers like Google Cloud with their TPUs and AWS with Trainium chips, but our full-stack control—from silicon to software—gives us a distinct edge.

On the cost side, COGS grew 22% YoY to $14.2 billion, slightly outpacing our revenue growth, thanks to these levers. Depreciation and amortization, tied to our $28 billion in capex this fiscal year—primarily for AI GPU clusters and edge locations—pressured margins by about 50 basis points. However, as these assets ramp, we expect utilization to push 90% by year-end, unlocking further expansion.

Regionally, in the Americas, which drove 52% of revenue, gross margins hit 35.2%—our strongest ever—fueled by hyperscaler demand from the Magnificent Seven and enterprise migrations. US East and West regions saw 90%+ utilization on NVIDIA H100/H200 clusters. EMEA, at 22% of revenue, expanded to 31.5% margins, up 200 bps YoY, as we optimized post-Brexit supply chains and expanded Frankfurt and Paris zones. Challenges persist in APAC, where margins compressed to 29.8% from aggressive capacity builds in Singapore, Tokyo, and new Mumbai-2 availability zones to capture 35% YoY growth. Here, bandwidth costs rose 10% due to undersea cable constraints, but our strategic partnerships with telcos like Reliance Jio are stabilizing this. China remains a non-GAAP adjustment, but our Alibaba Cloud collaboration is yielding 40% margins on compliant offerings.

Strategically, these trends validate our invest-now-win-later thesis on AI infrastructure. RPO grew 42% YoY to $165 billion, with 60% weighted toward multi-year AI contracts, providing visibility into margin tailwinds. We're also advancing zero-trust efficiency programs, like our Auto Scaling Groups with predictive ML for idle capacity reclamation, which shaved 8% off compute waste. Compared to peers, our 32.8% trails AWS's reported 30-31% but outpaces Azure's mid-20s on a services-adjusted basis, reflecting our purer cloud focus without legacy drag.

Looking forward, we guide Q3 gross margins to 33.0-33.5%, with full-year expansion to 33.5%. Risks include GPU supply chain tightness—NVIDIA Blackwell ramps are delayed to Q4—and potential pricing pressure from startups like CoreWeave, but our ecosystem moat via integrations with Snowflake, Databricks, and Hugging Face positions us for premium capture. In summary, our gross margin trajectory is resilient, driven by mix, efficiency, and scale—setting the stage for 1,000 bps+ expansion over the next five years as AI becomes the new OS of enterprise.

Next, I'd like to introduce Dr. Elena Vasquez, who will provide an update on our technology strategy and roadmap.

Dr. Elena Vasquez:
Thank you, Michael. We are committed to leading the way in cloud technology innovation. We are making significant investments in research and development to create cutting-edge solutions for our customers.

Today, I'd like to dive deep into one of the key drivers behind our record performance: the impact of our pricing strategies and discounting programs. In a hyper-competitive cloud landscape dominated by hyperscalers like AWS, Azure, and Google Cloud, where customers are increasingly multi-cloud savvy and cost-sensitive, our disciplined approach to pricing has not only accelerated net new bookings by 28% year-over-year but also improved our average revenue per user—or ARPU—by 12% to $1.45 million annually for enterprise accounts.

Our core pricing pillars include on-demand pay-as-you-go, Reserved Instances, Savings Plans, and Spot Instances, supplemented by targeted discounting for volume commitments, competitive displacements, and strategic bundles.

Revenue mix and ARPU dynamics show in our compute and storage revenue. On-demand usage, which carries our highest margins at around 75% gross margin, grew 18% quarter-over-quarter, fueled by bursty AI/ML workloads on our Nimbus ML platform—think GPU-accelerated training runs for large language models similar to those on AWS EC2 P5 instances. However, the real margin expander has been our shift toward committed contracts. RIs and Savings Plans now represent 52% of total compute revenue, up from 42% a year ago, delivering an average 35-55% discount off on-demand rates for 1- or 3-year terms. This mix shift contributed $450 million in annualized recurring revenue from new commitments in Q3 alone, offsetting any pricing pressure from macroeconomic headwinds.

ARPU growth was particularly strong in high-value workloads. For customers running Kubernetes-orchestrated container fleets on our Nimbus Kubernetes Engine, bundling with premium features like auto-scaling and serverless functions boosted effective pricing by 15%. We saw this in deals with Fortune 500 names in financial services, where ARPU hit $2.8 million, compared to the industry average of $1.2 million per Gartner data.

Discounting remains a precision tool, applied judiciously to win multi-year deals and defend against poaching. In Q3, we issued $1.2 billion in discounts across 1,400 enterprise accounts, a 22% increase YoY, but with a net positive impact on lifetime value. Our dynamic discounting model—powered by ML algorithms analyzing customer telemetry, like utilization rates and egress patterns—targets 20-40% off for 70%+ utilization commitments, yielding a 3x ROI within 18 months via reduced churn.

Key wins included displacing Azure in 15% of competitive deals, where we offered hybrid discounts: 45% off RIs plus free data transfer for the first 12 months on our Nimbus Data Lake, mirroring AWS's Outposts pricing incentives. This strategy netted us $320 million in net new ARR from migrations, with payback periods averaging 9 months. For SMBs and startups, our Spot Instance discounts—up to 90% off for interruptible workloads—drove 35% growth in that segment, capturing dev/test environments akin to Google Cloud's preemptible VMs.

Economically, discounting compressed our overall cloud gross margin by 220 basis points to 68%, but this was more than offset by a 15% uplift in dollar-based net retention rate to 128%. Without these programs, we'd estimate a 5-7% drag on bookings growth amid the current environment of elevated interest rates and IT budget scrutiny.

Geographically, pricing strategies played out differently. In North America, our mature market at 65% of revenue, we leaned conservative: average discounts at 25%, emphasizing value-based pricing for sovereign AI clouds amid U.S. CHIPS Act subsidies. This preserved margins at 72% while growing enterprise ACVs by 20%.

APAC was aggressive, with discounts averaging 38% to penetrate hyperscaler strongholds. In India, where AWS holds 32% share per IDC, our Nimbus Frontier program offered 50% off for 3-year RIs on Mumbai and Singapore regions, driving 45% YoY revenue growth and flipping 200 accounts from Azure. China remains nascent at 4% of revenue, but localized pricing parity with Alibaba Cloud—capped at 30% discounts—secured pilots with state-owned enterprises, positioning us for 50% growth in FY25.

EMEA saw balanced play: GDPR-compliant discounts bundled with our Nimbus Confidential Compute enclaves like AWS Nitro won EU public sector deals, up 30% YoY, though pricing pressure from OVHcloud tempered ARPU gains to 8%.

Underpinning this is our AI-driven pricing engine, NimbusOptix, which uses reinforcement learning on 10 petabytes of anonymized usage data to predict elasticity and auto-tender personalized Savings Plans—reducing quote-to-cash cycles by 40%. We're also piloting outcome-based pricing for AI workloads: pay-per-token generated on NimbusML, similar to OpenAI's API model but integrated with our infra stack, targeting 20% uptake by year-end.

Looking ahead, trends favor us. Synergy Research shows committed contract adoption rising from 40% to 55% industry-wide as CFOs lock in rates amid 5-10% on-demand hikes from peers. Multi-cloud complexity is pushing price normalization tools, where we discount 15% for unified billing across Nimbus, AWS, and Azure via our MultiNimbus Orchestrator.

In summary, our pricing and discounting have turbocharged growth without sacrificing profitability—adding 400 basis points to our Rule of 40 score at 68. We expect this momentum to sustain, with Q4 committed bookings guidance at $1.5 billion, supporting our raised FY24 revenue outlook of $28-29 billion, up 24% at the midpoint.

Now, I'll pass it over to Jordan Lee to discuss our product roadmap and recent launches.

Jordan Lee:
Thank you, Elena. We recently launched Nimbus EdgeForge, a groundbreaking solution designed to revolutionize edge computing for telco and retail.

Good afternoon, everyone. Before diving into forward guidance, I'd like to unpack our customer churn rate and retention trends, which remain a cornerstone of our multi-year growth story in the cloud computing landscape. In our IaaS, PaaS, and SaaS-heavy portfolio—spanning core infrastructure like our Kubernetes-orchestrated compute clusters, object storage akin to S3, and specialized AI/ML platforms—we measure success not just by new logo wins, but by the stickiness of our deployments and the expansion within our 28,000+ customer base.

Headline metrics: Our dollar-based net retention rate, or NRR, came in at 118% for Q3, marking a 300 basis point improvement year-over-year from 115%, and up sequentially from 116%. This continues our streak of 10 consecutive quarters above 115%, well ahead of the public cloud peer average of around 110% as reported by companies like Snowflake and Datadog. NRR captures both our gross retention—revenue retained from existing cohorts excluding expansions—and the net impact of upsells, cross-sells, and pricing optimizations. Drilling down, our gross dollar retention rate held steady at 92%, reflecting minimal contraction even amid macroeconomic headwinds like elevated interest rates and selective IT spend in non-mission-critical workloads.

On churn specifically, our annualized dollar churn rate improved to 4.8% in Q3, down from 6.2% a year ago and 5.1% prior quarter. This translates to just under 5% logo churn for the quarter, heavily skewed toward our smaller SMB cohort. Enterprise customers—those with ACV over $1 million, representing 42% of our ARR—posted a razor-thin churn rate of 2.9%, versus 7.5% for SMBs under $100K ACV. This segmentation mirrors industry patterns we've seen at hyperscalers like AWS and Azure, where Fortune 500 workloads become deeply entrenched due to data gravity and refactoring costs.

Regionally, retention trends paint an optimistic picture. In the Americas, accounting for 58% of our ARR, NRR expanded to 122%, driven by hyperscale expansions in AI training workloads—think customers like a major U.S. bank scaling our GPU-accelerated inference services 3x YoY. EMEA followed at 115% NRR, bolstered by GDPR-compliant sovereign cloud offerings that helped us retain 95% of our public sector cohort amid regulatory shifts. APAC, our fastest-growing region at 22% YoY ARR growth, saw NRR at 110%—solid but lagging due to fiercer competition from Alibaba Cloud and Tencent in China, where we lost 1.2 points of retention from pricing pressures on commodity storage. That said, our APAC churn stabilized at 6.1% annualized after peaking at 8% last year, thanks to localized edge computing POPs in Singapore and Sydney.

What's driving these trends? Technical initiatives that enhance platform lock-in. We've accelerated our NimbusLock customer success program, which includes automated migration tools for VMware workloads—converting over 1,200 customers to our native hypervisor in Q3 alone, reducing egress fees by an average 25%. Our integration with open-source ecosystems like CNCF's Falco for security observability has cut mean-time-to-resolution for incidents by 40%, directly correlating to a 15% lower churn risk per internal cohort analysis. On the AI front, the launch of Nimbus AI Studio—our serverless endpoint for fine-tuned LLMs compatible with Hugging Face models—drove 28% of Q3 expansions, as customers consolidate from multi-cloud setups with Azure OpenAI or Google Vertex AI.

Strategically, we're doubling down on land-and-expand dynamics tailored to cloud economics. Economic uncertainty has made CIOs prioritize consumption-based pricing, so we optimized our committed use discounts in Q3, offering 20-30% savings for three-year commitments on sustained-use compute—resulting in $450 million in new multi-year contracts, extending our RPO visibility to 14 months. We've also invested in proactive churn prediction via our internal ML models, flagging at-risk accounts 90 days early with 87% accuracy; this intervention retained $120 million in ARR at risk this quarter. Competitively, while AWS dominates IaaS market share at ~32% per Synergy Research, our focus on mid-market PaaS niches—like composable data pipelines rivaling Snowflake's Snowpark—has widened our NRR moat to 8 points above the median SaaS peer.

Looking ahead, we expect Q4 NRR to hold in the 117-119% band, with churn trending toward 4.5% annualized, supported by our $200 million customer success expansion and new sustainability commitments—like carbon-neutral regions in EU-West-1—that resonate with ESG-focused enterprises. Risks remain, including potential slowdowns in non-AI capex as seen in recent Oracle Cloud guidance, but our 92% gross retention underscores the durability of cloud workloads once landed.

In summary, our retention metrics affirm Nimbus Cloud's position as a high-velocity cloud leader, with NRR compounding our 28% YoY ARR growth.

I'll now hand it over to Taylor Kim to provide an update on our marketing initiatives and brand strategy.

Taylor Kim:
Thank you, Jordan. Our marketing efforts are focused on building brand awareness and driving demand for our innovative solutions.

Before we dive into the segment details, I want to address a key factor influencing our top-line results this quarter: the impact of currency fluctuations on revenue. As a truly global cloud leader with over 55% of our $28.7 billion in Q3 revenue coming from outside the U.S., we're naturally exposed to FX volatility. And in Q3, a strengthening U.S. dollar created a meaningful headwind, which I'll break down with specifics, regional insights, and our mitigation strategies.

First, the headline numbers. On a reported basis, total revenue grew 32% year-over-year to $28.7 billion, driven by robust demand for our core IaaS and PaaS offerings like Nimbus Compute, Nimbus Storage, and our AI-optimized Nimbus ML workloads. However, on a constant currency basis, growth was even stronger at 35%. FX fluctuations shaved approximately 3 percentage points off our reported growth, equating to a $780 million headwind—or about 3% of total revenue. This compares to a $450 million tailwind in Q3 FY2023 when the dollar was weaker, highlighting the swing potential in our international book.

Regional impacts: EMEA, which represented 28% of Q3 revenue at $8.2 billion (up 38% reported, 42% constant currency), bore the brunt due to the euro's 8% depreciation against the USD over the quarter. Key markets like Germany and the UK saw our Azure-competitive Nimbus Kubernetes services and VMware-alternative Nimbus Virtual Private Cloud usage surge amid enterprise migrations, but the EUR/USD rate averaging 1.08—down from 1.15 last year—translated to a $320 million revenue drag. In France and the Nordics, where we're ramping sovereign cloud initiatives compliant with GDPR and the EU Data Act, local currency contracts mitigated some pain, but spot-market usage billing exposed us more.

APAC, our fastest-growing region at 22% of revenue or $6.4 billion (52% reported growth, 57% constant currency), the yen's 12% slide against the dollar hit hardest. Japan alone, a powerhouse for our Nimbus Edge Computing tied to 5G rollouts with partners like SoftBank, contributed a $210 million FX headwind. Australia and India fared better with the AUD holding steadier, but overall, APAC's usage-based revenue—think high-velocity AI training on Nimbus GPUs—magnifies FX swings since bills are often denominated in USD for hyperscale customers like regional banks adopting our FinOps tools.

LATAM and Canada rounded out the international exposure at 12% of revenue, or $3.45 billion, with a milder $150 million headwind from BRL and CAD weakness. Brazil's public sector cloud tenders, mirroring AWS's Outposts deployments, provided some offset via local currency indexing.

Historically, over the past eight quarters, cumulative FX volatility has impacted reported revenue by plus or minus 2-4% annually. Our TTM average hedge covers 65% of forecasted international exposure, up from 50% two years ago, using forward contracts, collars, and FX options on a rolling 12-18 month basis. In Q3, hedges captured $220 million in gains, softening the net impact to $560 million.

Strategically, we're not just hedging financially; we're operationalizing against FX risks in ways unique to cloud dynamics. We've accelerated local currency billing: 72% of new EMEA and APAC contracts now bill in native currencies like EUR, JPY, or INR, up from 55% last year, reducing translation exposure on our $150 billion+ annualized run-rate. Dynamic pricing algorithms in our Nimbus Billing Console auto-adjust for FX thresholds—e.g., a 5% monthly depreciation triggers a 2-3% local price uplift, preserving ARPU without churn, as evidenced by our 92% gross retention rate.

On the infrastructure side, Q3 saw us light up 15 new edge zones in APAC, including Seoul and Mumbai, cutting latency for Jio and SoftBank workloads while matching regional currencies. This supports our multi-region DRaaS play, which grew 45% YoY. Looking ahead, as we integrate generative AI via Nimbus Bedrock-like foundation models, we'll tie pricing more to local compute capacity, further de-risking.

Forward guidance reflects this: For Q4, we expect a $600-700 million FX headwind assuming current forwards, implying 30-32% reported growth versus 33-35% constant currency on $29.5-30.5 billion revenue. Sensitivity: A 10% further USD appreciation would add $400 million pressure, but our hedges cover 70% at current levels.

In summary, while FX headwinds masked some of our underlying momentum this quarter—particularly in high-growth AI and edge workloads—our diversified revenue streams, proactive hedging, and cloud-native mitigations position us resiliently. We're capturing share in a $600 billion TAM, much like peers AWS and Azure, and FX noise won't derail our path to $112-113 billion FY2024 revenue.

Next, I'd like to introduce Ryan Brooks, who will discuss our sales performance and customer acquisition strategies.

Ryan Brooks:
Thank you, Taylor. Our sales team has been instrumental in driving our strong growth in the Q3 FY2024. We are focused on expanding our customer base and strengthening our existing relationships.

As we dive deeper into the financials, I'd like to turn to our new customer acquisition cost, or CAC, analysis—a critical metric for understanding the efficiency of our go-to-market engine in this hyper-competitive cloud landscape. CAC is calculated as our total sales and marketing expenses divided by the number of new customers added during the period. We track it on a blended basis but break it out by customer cohort—enterprise (those with $1M+ ARR commitments), mid-market ($100K-$1M ARR), and SMB (under $100K ARR)—to reflect the diverse dynamics of cloud adoption.

In Q3, our blended CAC came in at $42,500 per new customer, a 12% sequential improvement from $48,200 prior quarter and a robust 18% year-over-year decline from $51,800. This marks our sixth straight quarter of CAC compression, driven by a mix of scale efficiencies, channel optimization, and a favorable shift in our customer mix toward higher-velocity mid-market wins. For context, this puts us at the lower end of the peer set—think along the lines of Snowflake's reported sub-$50K enterprise CAC or Datadog's efficient mid-market model—while we continue to outpace pure-play hyperscalers like AWS or Azure, whose sales motions remain heavier on field-led deals.

Regionally, geography plays a huge role. North America (65% of new logos): CAC here was $38,000, down 15% YoY. The U.S. enterprise segment benefited from our expanded partner ecosystem—we ramped alliances with 25 new SIs like Accenture and Deloitte, contributing to 28% of NA new customers via indirect channels. Mid-market CAC dropped to $22K on the back of our Nimbus Accelerate program, which bundles our AI-optimized Kubernetes services with free migrations from EKS or AKS, shortening sales cycles from 120 to 75 days.

EMEA (22% of new logos): At $52,000, this was our highest but improved 10% YoY thanks to GDPR-compliant edge computing wins. Key here was landing 12 sovereign cloud deals in Germany and France, leveraging our Nimbus Edge Fabric—similar to AWS Outposts but with lower latency for telco 5G workloads. SMB CAC fell 22% to $15K via localized inbound campaigns targeting SAP HANA migrations.

APAC (13% of new logos): CAC stabilized at $46,000, flat YoY but with upside potential. Japan and India drove growth, where we acquired 40 new mid-market customers via hyperscaler partnerships—think multi-cloud integrations with Azure Arc and Google Anthos. Challenges persist in China due to regulatory hurdles, but our Singapore hub is yielding 30-day payback on SMB trials.

Segment-wise: Enterprise CAC held steady at $95,000—still elevated due to complex RFPs and proofs-of-concept for our Nimbus AI Foundry platform, which competes head-on with AWS SageMaker and Azure OpenAI. But payback remains stellar at 9 months, with LTV:CAC ratios exceeding 5:1 on 140% NDR from expansions into generative AI workloads. Mid-market is our efficiency star at $25,000 CAC (down 20% YoY), fueled by self-serve onboarding and our Pay-as-You-Grow consumption model, mirroring MongoDB Atlas's playbook. SMB CAC plummeted to $12,500 (25% YoY decline) via viral freemium tiers, akin to GCP's free credits but extended to 90 days with GPU bursts for ML prototyping.

Driving this compression: AI-powered sales tools, including our proprietary Nimbus Sales Copilot—built on our own LLMs—which automates 40% of lead scoring and demo personalization, reducing variable sales costs by 16%. Integration with Salesforce Einstein and HubSpot has cut qualification time by 35%.

Channel and inbound scale: Channels now account for 35% of new ARR (up from 22% YoY), with payback under 6 months. Our marketplace listings on AWS and Azure Marketplaces generated $18M in partner-led pipeline. Inbound marketing—whitepapers on multi-cloud cost optimization amid the post-ChatGPT AI boom—drove 52% of mid-market leads, at just $4K CAC.

Product-led growth enhancements: Adoption of our Nimbus Free Tier exploded 3x YoY, converting 18% to paid (vs. AWS's 12-15% industry benchmark). Usage-based pricing for serverless functions and vector databases has lowered barriers, especially for startups building on our Neon DB-compatible Postgres.

Looking ahead, we expect Q4 blended CAC to dip another 8-10% to the $38K-$39K range, supported by $50M in committed channel incentives and further AI automation. CAC payback sits at a healthy 8.2 months (enterprise: 9.5; mid-market: 6.8), with LTV:CAC at 4.8x overall. Risks include hyperscaler price wars—AWS's recent 15% EC2 cuts pressured margins—but our focus on differentiated AI infrastructure positions us for rule-of-40 expansion.

In summary, our CAC trajectory reflects disciplined execution in a market where AI is accelerating cloud migrations but lengthening enterprise scrutiny. We're not just acquiring customers cheaper; we're acquiring stickier, higher-LTV ones.

Now, I'll pass it over to Lisa Wong to discuss our security initiatives and commitment to data protection.

Lisa Wong:
Thank you, Ryan. Security is paramount to our mission. We are committed to protecting our customers' data and ensuring the integrity of our cloud platform.

I'll now dive into our Average Revenue Per User—or ARPU—metrics, which continue to underscore the strength of our customer expansion and monetization strategies in the cloud computing landscape. We define ARPU as total revenue divided by our average monthly active customer accounts over the quarter, annualized for clarity. This metric is a key leading indicator of wallet share capture, particularly as enterprises deepen their commitments to hybrid multi-cloud architectures, AI/ML workloads, and data-intensive applications.
